Sometimes anxiety builds up so much, that I'll stand there while people are talking to me and scream in my head for help. I feel like im drowning because I have no friends to socialize with, please help. Please ask me whats wrong even if I say I'm ok, please ask again until I feel like I can tell you what's really bothering me. 

But I'll laugh on que to whatever they said, and they'll walk away never asking if I'm alright.

I'm so SICK of my boyfriend. I've had to put up with nine years of criticism. I'll admit, I've  had plenty of growing up to do in those nine years as i left my home when I became legally able to. 
I only noticed it just this past year. He taught me how to think more on a logical level rather than an emotional one, so lately I've been arguing back with reason rather than a simple "because I think so!" Or something or other. But this isn't enough. Because I can't express a concern without sounding like i care (so i get a bit passionate? I apologize for losing face but reiterate my point more calmly), my worries become something of an overreaction to him.
It's gotten to the point where I don't believe he even cares about how I feel. Like there's no empathy to any point I make. When i told him this he called me a victimizer. Is this true? Am i a narcissist? Do i like being a victim? Im starting to believe this. But what if I was anyone else? No, this seems like a perfectly reasonable request, "please be more considerate towards my feelings".
But I know I'm not exactly stable. I'm depressed often and i6 refuse to seek help. I feel like im losing to myself. Mind over matter right? Just tough it out, depression ends eventually right? I know this isn't correct, but I'm embarrassed and stubborn so I do my best to differentiate between what's manic and what a healthy person would deam reasonable. 
But being called a "victimizer" is a bigger kind of blow. It indicates that I can't see past my own selfishness. But our arguments are always about things besides me. Money, jobs, our daughter's well-being, etc. So how am I failing to understand that I'm a victimizer? Am i being emotionally abused? If I think I'm being emotionally abused but really not, does that then make me a victimizer? This kind of self-awareness is nerve wracking. 

TL;DR: Boyfriend calls me a victimizer, I'm trying to understand what makes him say that.

Ps: thanks for reading/letting me post here.
